item.title: Rangers Petition CAF Over Disorderly Conduct Of MC Alger Fans During Champions League Match
item.description: Rangers International FC of Enugu has petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) following incidents, including vandalism, involving visiting supporters of MC Alger during and after the CAF Champions League fixture at the MKO Abiola Stadium, Abeokuta, on Sunday, 18 October 2026. The club raised concerns regarding the reported destruction of a stadium entrance gate, unauthorised entry without payment of gate fees, vandalisation of stadium seats and other acts of disorder. “Rangers International FC, Enugu, confirms that it has formally petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) following incidents involving visiting supporters during and after our CAF Champions League fixture against MC Alger at the MKO Abiola Stadium, Abeokuta, on Sunday, 18 October 2026,” it said in a statement posted on its X handle. Rangers have won the Nigerian title nine times. Photo: CAF Online In its petition, Rangers requested urgent intervention by CAF, including consideration of appropriate precautionary measures ahead of the return fixture scheduled for Friday, 23 October 2026, in Algiers, the capital of Algeria. “Rangers International FC remains committed to fair play, respect for football regulations and the safety of players, officials, supporters and all stakeholders,” the club stated. “We have confidence in the established processes of CAF and await its response. We thank our supporters for their continued loyalty and urge everyone to remain calm, disciplined and focused as the Club prepares for the return leg. Never Say Die.” The Enugu-based outfit beat MC Alger 2-0 in the first leg of their Champions League second preliminary round clash. The Flying Antelopes played with 10 men from the 13th minute of the clash at the MKO Abiola Sports Complex in Abeokuta, Ogun State, but scored in the 84th and 87th minutes to secure victory over their Algerian opponent. MC Alger had defeated ASN Nigelec of Niger Republic 5-0 on aggregate to qualify for the next stage. The Algerians won the domestic title and are seen as a formidable opponent for Rangers. The winner of the two-legged tie between Rangers and MC Alger will book a place in the 2026/27 group stage. item.title: JAMB warns universities against issuing admission letters
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, has warned universities in the country against issuing admission letters to candidates seeking admission into their various institutions, insisting that such act was not within their mandate to do so. The registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, stated this when he received a delegation from Veritas University, Bwari, Abuja, which paid him a courtesy visit in his office. According to the registrar, JAMB is the only body statutorily empowered to issue official admission letters to candidates seeking entry into all tertiary institutions in Nigeria, including universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education. Prof. Aina stated that the irony of the situation is that once candidates see a document as emanating from an institution purporting to offer them admission, they believe that it is real. He, therefore, charged universities guilty of this ignoble act to desist, adding that they also have the responsibility of ensuring that those candidates obtain the right documents from the board. Furthermore, he recalled that the Federal Ministry of Education had explicitly mandated that all admissions be conducted through the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) and that anything done contrary to that is illegal and invalid. As a consequence, no institution is permitted to substitute its own letters for the official JAMB admission letter issued by the board after a candidate had accepted his admission on CAPS. He added that it is only admission offered through this platform is recognised and would be accepted for the purpose of mobilisation for the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), among others. item.title: Photos: COAS visits Rwanda genocide memorial, urges national unity
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has highlighted the importance of national unity, religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence following his visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial in Rwanda. Shaibu, who visited the memorial on Monday as part of his ongoing working visit to Rwanda, said the country’s tragic history offered important lessons on the devastating consequences of ethnic hatred, divisive rhetoric and violent extremism. The Kigali Genocide Memorial houses the remains of approximately 250,000 victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, serving as a solemn reminder of the dangers of unchecked hatred, political manipulation and national disunity. A statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the visit underscored the need for Nigerians to rise above ethnic, religious and political differences in the collective pursuit of national peace and stability. The statement noted that Rwanda’s experience reinforced the importance of rejecting hate speech, embracing tolerance and promoting patriotism and collective responsibility among citizens. It added that the visit highlighted the critical roles of responsible leadership, early conflict prevention and sustained civil-military cooperation in preventing violent conflicts and strengthening national cohesion. The Nigerian Army chief’s visit comes amid continuing security challenges in Nigeria, reinforcing the importance of unity and collaboration in addressing threats to national peace and stability. The Army reiterated that national unity remains fundamental to achieving enduring peace, security and sustainable development. item.title: FG backtracks on recruitment waivers for varsities, clarifies approval process
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has clarified that federal tertiary institutions must continue to obtain recruitment waivers before employing additional personnel, amid confusion triggered by a presidential representative’s recent announcement at a university convocation. The Federal Ministry of Education, in a statement issued by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, on Monday, said the recruitment waiver process remained in force, contrary to impressions created by remarks delivered on behalf of President Bola Tinubu at the maiden convocation of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Azare, on October 17, 2026. The clarification effectively draws a distinction between the approval of staff establishments and the authorisation to recruit, insisting that neither process has been scrapped. According to the ministry, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF) retains the responsibility for approving establishment waivers, determining authorised staff strength and assessing manpower requirements across federal institutions. However, requests by tertiary institutions to recruit beyond their approved establishments are considered by a separate committee chaired by the Minister of Education. The ministry explained that the committee evaluates institutions’ staffing needs against their approved establishments before determining whether additional recruitment is justified. The OHCSF is also represented on the committee, ensuring that recruitment requests are assessed in line with approved manpower structures and existing procedures. It said the arrangement, which has operated over the past few years, was designed to promote institutional efficiency and autonomy without abandoning established controls over public-sector recruitment. “All requests must continue to comply strictly with the established approval process,” the ministry stressed. The clarification comes after the presidential representative’s remarks at the Azare convocation generated the impression that federal tertiary institutions had been freed from the requirement to obtain recruitment waivers through the existing framework. Reaffirming its commitment to transparency, due process and accountability, the ministry said the continued application of the protocol was consistent with the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) and Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The statement did not indicate any new policy change, but stressed that the existing arrangements governing recruitment approvals in federal tertiary institutions remained operational. item.title: England women’s coach Wiegman signs two-year contract extension
item.description: England women’s head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension, taking her through until the end of the 2029 women’s European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday. Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021. The 56-year-old Dutchwoman has reached five successive major tournament finals, also winning Euro 2017 with her native Netherlands. “I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” Wiegman said Monday. England, beaten by Spain in the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year’s tournament in Brazil. “Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come,” Wiegman added. “We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.” Wiegman’s new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. item.title: Gunmen shoot Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, three suspects held
item.description: Indian actor Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai on Sunday, police said, adding that three suspects have been detained. Shooters opened fire at the 36-year-old actor as he was leaving a private event in the city’s upscale Juhu area on Sunday evening, according to Police official Mohit Garg. Aside from being India’s financial capital, Mumbai is also the heart of Bollywood, the country’s Hindi-language film industry. “Tiger Shroff is safe and Mumbai police has deployed different teams to investigate further,” Garg told reporters. Two people were injured in the incident, including the actor’s driver, though Shroff did not sustain gunshot wounds, police said. Three suspects have been rounded up in Rajasthan, another Indian state. “Preliminary questioning revealed that two of them have one case each against them, one related to theft and the other under the Arms Act,” police official Tejaswani Gautam told reporters. Police have yet to establish a motive for the shooting. Shroff is known for action films including the “Baaghi” franchise and “War”. item.title: Musk says will give SpaceX share to ‘every kid in America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Monday that he would give every child in the United States a share in his SpaceX rocket company. “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk, the richest man in the world, said on X. “This will be the first of many,” he said, without providing details about how the scheme would work. There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau. Musk owns 38 percent of SpaceX, according to Forbes. His announcement comes after President Donald Trump promised last month to give every American adult $5,000 if his Republican party retains control of Congress in November’s midterm elections. SpaceX set the record for the largest initial public offering in history, raising $85.7 billion in June. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk’s Mars ambitions. item.title: Bauchi: Witchcraft claim sparks violent attack as police arrest 17
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi state police command has arrested 17 suspects over an alleged witchcraft accusation that triggered a violent attack on a family in Gobirawa Village, Alkaleri Local Government Area of the state. The suspects allegedly attacked a 60-year-old man and his family after accusing the man’s son of witchcraft following the death of a 20-year-old resident, identified as Halilu Ahmad, on October 16, 2026. The incident occurred around 1am on October 18, when the suspects allegedly invaded the victim’s residence armed with machetes and sticks, inflicting multiple injuries on him and his 30-year-old son. The attackers were also alleged to have damaged two motorcycles belonging to the family. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the attack was triggered by the suspects’ belief that the victim’s son was responsible for the death through witchcraft. Due to the deteriorating condition of the 60-year-old victim, he was initially taken to General Hospital, Alkaleri, before being referred to Ihsan Hospital, Bauchi, for further treatment. Police spokesman SP Nafiu Habib, who disclosed this in a statement on Monday, said detectives attached to Alkaleri Division arrested the 17 suspects following the incident. He said the commissioner of police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, had directed the transfer of the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Bauchi, for discreet investigation and the arrest of three other suspects still at large. The police spokesman quoted the commissioner as warning against accusations of witchcraft and other unverified superstitious beliefs that could lead to violence and the unlawful punishment of innocent persons. Aliyu urged residents to report suspicions, grievances and criminal allegations to the police rather than resorting to self-help or jungle justice. He assured the public that the command would pursue justice in the case and would not tolerate actions capable of threatening public peace and security. Airstrikes continue on a daily basis. People continue to be displaced,” Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, told AFP at the agency’s office in east Jerusalem. “Almost everybody remains without a permanent home to live in. item.title: African players in Europe: Mbeumo goal eases pressure on Carrick
item.description: Cameroon star Bryan Mbeumo scored his fourth Premier League goal this season for struggling Manchester United in a 1-1 away draw against Leeds United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND BRYAN MBEUMO (Manchester United) Mbeumo netted to ensure under-fire United boss Michael Carrick did not suffer another damaging defeat. Mbeumo put United ahead in the 35th minute against bitter rivals Leeds at Elland Road as he slotted home a Youri Tielemans cross. Leeds hit back to rescue a draw thanks to Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s second-half goal, but avoiding defeat was vital for Carrick after United’s poor start to the season. ALEX IWOBI (Fulham) The Nigeria midfielder’s first goal since March clinched a maiden Premier League win for Cottagers boss Alvaro Arbeloa. Iwobi netted in the 33rd minute of the 1-0 win against Hull at Craven Cottage, taking Sander Berge’s pass and hitting a low strike that squirmed under Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. That was enough to lift Fulham out of the relegation zone and give former Real Madrid manager Arbeloa some much-needed breathing space. SPAIN EZ ABDE (Real Betis) Morocco international Abde scored against his former side Barcelona in Real Betis’s pulsating 5-2 La Liga defeat. The 24-year-old winger produced a sharp finish early in the second half for his fourth goal in his last five matches for the Andalucian side. BIL NSONGO (Deportivo La Coruna) Deportivo La Coruna striker Nsongo netted his first goal of the season to secure the Galician outfit a point against Levante in a 1-1 draw. The 22-year-old Cameroon international reacted quickest to reach a rebound in the box and bundle the ball home. ITALY AKOR ADAMS (Venezia) Nigerian Adams scored as bottom club Venezia ended a six-match losing steak since the Serie A season began by defeating former champions Napoli 1-0. New Venezia head coach Davide Nicola made a dream debut as Adams latched on to a long ball and scored with a deflected strike after 49 minutes. ANGE-YOAN BONNY (Inter Milan) The Ivory Coast forward wrapped up a 3-1 win for defending champions Inter Milan away to Bologna by scoring six minutes from time. Bonny netted after being set up by fellow substitute and scorer Carlos Augusto. GERMANY IBRAHIM MAZA (Bayer Leverkusen) Leverkusen midfielder Maza continued his impressive development with a goal and an assist in a 2-1 Bundesliga home win over Freiburg. The Algerian turned in a Patrik Schick pass midway through the opening half and then created a goal for the Czech with an excellent dribble late in the game. Named man of the match, Maza said he was “building chemistry” with veteran striker Schick, the first Bayer player to score in the first six games of the season. item.title: Four Soldiers Dead, Dozens Injured In Canada Military Base Fire
item.description: Four soldiers were killed, and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada’s armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday. Carney made the solemn announcement without providing details on what caused the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright on Saturday. “It is with deep sadness that I can confirm, at this time, that four service members have lost their lives and that their loved ones have been notified,” Carney said in the capital Ottawa, adding that “dozens of others have been seriously injured.” “This is one of the worst tragedies the Canadian Armed Forces have experienced on Canadian soil in peacetime,” he said. item.title: Wike, Rivers lawmakers meet Fubara
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, Port Harcourt The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has led members of the Rivers State House of Assembly and local government chairmen in the state to a closed-door meeting with the Governor of the state, Siminalayi Fubara. The meeting, whose agenda has not been ascertained, was held at the primate residence of Fubara in Port Harcourt, Sunday evening. The high-profile meeting marked the first time Wike and the lawmakers visited the governor at his residence. The minister had led the delegation, comprising mainly members of the state assembly, led by its speaker, Rt Hon Martin Amaewhule, the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Kingsley Chinda, and the state’s 23 local government chairmen, and other members of the Rainbow Coalition, to meet with the governor and his supporters. This was coming after an earlier meeting some weeks back in which Wike had also led members of the Rainbow Coalition in the state, including the candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections, Kingsley Chinda, to meet with Fubara. It was, however, gathered that the Sunday meeting was in continuation of talks between the camps of Wike and Fubara in order to build on the ongoing reconciliation efforts in the state. It was gathered that the meeting was to strengthen efforts to put the political crisis that rocked the state behind and explore ways of accommodating Fubara’s loyalists in the new political setting of 2027. It was learned that at the end of the engagement, Wike and Fubara came out with smiles, likewise the lawmakers, LG Chairmen and other members of the Rainbow Coalition. At the entrance door where they took pictures, the speaker, Amaewhule, and others were captured in a video greeting and shaking hands with the governor, bowing and calling ‘Your Excellency’ even as Fubara acknowledged the greetings with smiles and later rejoined his political godfather, Wike, before all posed for the group photograph. It would be recalled that Fubara and the Amaewhule-led House of Assembly had been entangled in deep war since the political crisis that lasted for over two years following a protracted disagreement between Fubara and his predecessor, Wike. The lawmakers during the heat of the political crisis had on two different occasions attempted to impeach the governor before President Bola Tinubu intervened with the declaration of a state of emergency, suspending the governor and others. Following the disagreement and in spite of the seeming reconciliation, the minister, who is the political leader of the team, ruled out a second tenure stance for Fubara and handed the ticket of the party to Chinda. However, at the verge of the 2027 poll, Wike has resumed moving to bring back all the leaders of his team from the two camps back together. item.title: 2027: Vote for candidate who’ll make your money buy more — Alaje advises Nigerians
item.description: Senior economist at SPM Professionals, Paul Alaje, has urged Nigerians to assess presidential candidates in the 2027 general election based on their ability to improve purchasing power, reduce living costs and make essential services more affordable. Alaje said voters should prioritise candidates whose economic policies would enable Nigerians to buy more with their earnings, rather than be swayed by promises of higher wages without corresponding improvements in real income. He made the remarks on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics while discussing the economic policies Nigerians should consider when evaluating candidates ahead of the 2027 presidential election. “Any candidate who is telling you that the money in your pocket will buy more, will improve more, and will afford your rent — that is the candidate you should vote for,” he said. The economist said an increase in nominal earnings would not necessarily translate into better living conditions if prices continued to rise faster than incomes. Explaining the concept of purchasing power, Alaje said Nigerians should consider what their earnings could buy and whether proposed economic policies would improve their ability to meet household needs. “You can earn more in naira terms. Like labour wants more money, you can. But will it buy more in real terms?” he asked. He said voters should examine candidates’ plans for making education more affordable, improving access to healthcare and addressing other pressures on household budgets. According to him, the central question should be which candidate can improve the real value of Nigerians’ earnings and make essential services accessible to more people. Alaje also warned that economic policies that fail to prioritise productivity could undermine the country’s economic performance. “Anybody who is not discussing productivity is going to run the economy down,” he said. He argued that productivity and other economic fundamentals must support reforms if they are to deliver sustainable improvements in living standards. 2027: Alaje urges Tinubu to address electricity The economist also called on President Bola Tinubu to take urgent steps to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, describing power supply as a critical factor in improving economic performance. “You need to do something urgent and critical about electricity,” he told the President. Alaje said countries that had successfully implemented reforms similar to Nigeria’s had underlying economic fundamentals that helped them achieve results. “Major economies that adopted the kind of reforms we are adopting and have results, they have fundamentals working for them,” he said. item.title: PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has declared seven days of mourning in honour of its leader and elder statesman, Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at the age of 86. Cole, popularly known as Chief PDC, died weeks after celebrating his 86th birthday, leaving behind a legacy of service in journalism, education, diplomacy, public administration and politics. In a statement signed by PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, on behalf of the organisation’s Board of Trustees (BoT) and National Executive Committee (NEC), the forum described Cole’s death as a painful and irreplaceable loss. Igali said Cole played significant roles in the socio-cultural and political development of the Niger Delta, particularly in the formation and growth of PANDEF. The late Cole served as Editor-in-Chief of the Daily Times of Nigeria, one of the country’s leading national newspapers, and later as presidential adviser on foreign affairs. He also served as Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil. According to Igali, Cole brought considerable intellectual depth and experience to various socio-cultural and socio-political organisations in the Niger Delta. PANDEF directed all its chapters in Nigeria and the diaspora to suspend official social activities for seven days, beginning October 18, 2026. It also directed that Cole’s photograph be displayed on its media platforms throughout the mourning period. Igali said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, noting that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a special adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. He added that Cole’s political choices were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people. Cole’s political career included a presidential bid under the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and membership of the Board of Trustees of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), PANDEF said. The forum also acknowledged his contributions as a Christian leader and advocate of Nigeria’s cultural heritage, particularly the traditions and identities of the South-South region. Expressing condolences over his death, PANDEF extended its sympathies to his son, Rt. Hon. Tonye Cole, other members of the Cole family, the people of Abonnema in the Kalabari Kingdom, the Ijaw nation, the Rivers State Government and the people of Rivers State, as well as Nigerians across the country. The organisation urged the bereaved family and the wider Niger Delta community to draw comfort from the distinguished life and enduring contributions of the late elder statesman. PANDEF prayed for the peaceful repose of Cole’s soul. The post PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: T hree people have been reportedly killed and several others injured in a renewed farmers-herders clash in Paikon-Kore community, Gwagwalada Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with houses and a motorcycle reportedly set ablaze. The violence, which began on Saturday afternoon and continued until Sunday morning, also left several shops at the Paikon-Kore village market burnt and goods destroyed. Experts urge that there is a need to nip the brewing crisis in the bud to avoid recurring deadly scenarios witnessed in other states like Benue and Plateau states, where farmers-herders clashes have claimed hundreds of lives and displaced many. A resident of the community, Danlami Ibrahim, said the clash started after some herders allegedly allowed their cattle into a groundnut farm whose crops were yet to be harvested. Ibrahim said the incident sparked anger among residents, particularly after other community members learnt of the farmer’s injury, leading to a reprisal in which three herders were reportedly killed. The violence, which began on Saturday afternoon and continued until Sunday morning, also left several shops at the Paikon-Kore village market burnt and goods destroyed. Experts urge that there is a need to nip the brewing crisis in the bud to avoid recurring deadly scenarios witnessed in other states like Benue and Plateau states, where farmers-herders clashes have claimed hundreds of lives and displaced many. A resident of the community, Danlami Ibrahim, said the clash started after some herders allegedly allowed their cattle into a groundnut farm whose crops were yet to be harvested. According to him, one of the herders allegedly brought out a cutlass and attacked a farmer, severing one of his hands. Ibrahim said the incident sparked anger among residents, particularly after other community members learnt of the farmer’s injury, leading to a reprisal in which three herders were reportedly killed. He added that two houses, several shops and a motorcycle were set ablaze during the violence. The resident said the clash continued until Sunday morning, leaving several people injured. Some of the victims were subsequently taken to hospitals in Gwagwalada for treatment. A visit to the affected village market by our correspondent showed several wooden, zinc-built and container shops burnt, with smoke still billowing from some of the shops. At Sabon Nakowa Hospital, a private medical facility in Gwagwalada, some victims were seen receiving treatment. Two others were also observed undergoing treatment at the accident and emergency unit of the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital. The Secretary of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Gwagwalada Area Council chapter, Mohammed Usman, said three herders lost their lives. “For now, information at my disposal shows that three herders lost their lives. That is what I can say for now, while I am yet to get the number of those who sustained injuries,” he said. Usman said he would provide further information as it became available, adding that he had informed the Gwagwalada Area Council chairman, Kasim Mohammed Ikwa, about the incident. Ikwa, who visited the affected community on Sunday alongside the Divisional Police Officer, SP Aaron H. Kaura, and other security operatives, condemned the renewed violence, describing it as unfortunate. He said the council would convene a stakeholders’ meeting on Monday (today) to deliberate on the crisis and seek ways to prevent further violence. The chairman urged both warring parties to embrace peace and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions. He also called on youths in Paikon-Kore to exercise restraint and promote peaceful coexistence with other residents, warning against confrontation and retaliatory attacks. Ikwa advised farmers whose crops were damaged by cattle to report such incidents to the relevant security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. He noted that such conflicts often affected innocent people who might not even understand the circumstances that triggered the dispute. The chairman further urged residents to cooperate with security personnel deployed to the community, adding that an expanded security meeting had been convened, with youth leaders, the Sarkin Noma and other community leaders from both sides invited to seek a lasting solution. Abari said he left the group for the Friday prayer at Banex Mosque, while Kashim and the others proceeded to Maitama Juma’at Mosque, popularly known as Yar’Adua Mosque. According to him, Kashim later took his friends home after the prayers and lunch before driving towards his residence in Asokoro, where the fatal accident occurred. Abari said the news of Kashim’s death was particularly shocking because the deceased was known to be an extremely careful driver. “One thing that is distinctive about him is that he is an extremely careful, cautious driver,” Abari said, adding that the same caution characterised the way Kashim approached his responsibilities. Describing him as a person who never flaunted his privileged family background, Abari said Kashim was well brought up, good-natured and friendly to people regardless of their social standing. “He was a personification of humility, never carrying any airs around him about the kind of family he came from,” he said. Abari added that although Kashim came from a political family and held his own political views, he never allowed political differences to damage his relationships with others. The former NOA director-general said the suddenness of the death was a reminder of the uncertainty of human life. “If I recall the moments we had together, I recall the banters, everything. He looked too far away from death. But we never knew that it was just hovering around,” he said. He prayed that Allah would forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. ‘We were friends for almost 50 years’ Yusuf, who said he had known Kashim for almost five decades, described him as a decent, dependable and God-fearing person. In his tribute, the former NHIS executive secretary said their friendship began at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and endured for nearly 50 years. “Arch. Shettima Mohammed Kashim and I met in ABU Zaria and have been very good friends for almost 50 years,” he said. Recounting their final hours together, Yusuf said they attended the book launch at the Yar’Adua Centre on Friday and left the venue at about 1:20pm. He said they proceeded to a mosque in Wuse II for the Friday prayer before having lunch at a nearby restaurant. They later observed the Asr prayer at the mosque before Kashim dropped him at his residence at about 4:30pm. Yusuf said he received a call from Kashim’s son about half an hour later, informing him that the family had been told that his father’s car was involved in an accident in Asokoro and that the occupant had been taken to Asokoro General Hospital. He said he rushed to the hospital, where he met members of Kashim’s family and brothers, who informed him that the architect had died. According to Yusuf, Kashim’s car ran into a stationary truck, resulting in fatal injuries. “Shettima Mohammed Kashim was more than a friend to me and many. He was a good, decent, dependable and God-fearing person,” he said. “May Allah forgive all his shortcomings and reward him with Jannatul Firdaus,” he prayed. Career as an architect Despite his family’s political background, Kashim maintained a professional career in architecture and public service, according to Abari. He said the deceased was trained as an architect and remained committed to his profession rather than using his family connections to pursue a political career. Abari recalled that Kashim served as general manager of the Borno Housing Corporation in the 1980s before moving to the federal service, where he also worked with the Federal Housing Authority. His career, Abari said, reflected a commitment to the profession in which he was trained. “He did not abandon his training as an architect,” he said. Kashim was also known by the traditional title of Shettima of Borno, a title associated with his family’s longstanding place in the traditional and political history of the region. Yusuf said the title had a historical connection to his father, Sir Kashim Ibrahim, who was conferred with the title of Shettima of Borno in 1935 and later became Waziri of Borno in 1956. Sir Kashim Ibrahim served as the first indigenous governor of the Northern Region of Nigeria from 1962 to 1966. Although his father occupied a prominent position in the country’s political history, Abari said Kashim remained approachable and maintained friendships with people of different backgrounds and political persuasions. Kashim was married to a daughter of the late Alhaji Mai Deribe, a renowned businessman.

item.title: ADAMAWA FOR ASIWAJU!
item.description: The Microphone Has Been Tested. The Signal Is Strong. The Structure Is Ready. Adamawa is ready, and its message is clear: the political structure, leadership and grassroots network are firmly in place to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. With Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri providing leadership, direction and strategic coordination, the state is prepared to pursue a decisive victory. The commitment is firm, the objective is clear, and the target is 100% electoral victory across the board. Achieving this goal requires sustained engagement, unity of purpose and disciplined organisation. Every stakeholder, coordinator and supporter has a role to play in taking the message to the people and translating commitment into votes. At the centre of this mobilisation is the Adamawa Renewed Hope 226 Movement (ARH-226M), led by its Director-General, Professor Abdullahi Liman Tukur. It is a structured, coordinated, knowledge-driven and grassroots-focused political movement established to transform political support into organised electoral action. Its reach extends across every level of the state’s political landscape: * 4,104 Polling Units: Where every vote counts and community engagement must translate into electoral participation. * 226 Electoral Wards: Where grassroots mobilisation takes shape, relationships are strengthened and local priorities receive attention. * 21 Local Government Areas: Where leadership, coordination and stakeholder engagement connect the statewide mission with community action. Through its 21 experienced LGA coordinators, clear leadership structures and effective mobilisation strategies, ARH-226M is prepared to reach communities, engage stakeholders and consolidate support for the APC from the polling units to the state level. The task is to sustain a visible presence, listen to the people, communicate the Renewed Hope message clearly and encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and confidently in the electoral process. From community meetings to stakeholder consultations, every engagement must strengthen trust, widen participation and reinforce a shared commitment to victory. With consistent follow-through and cooperation across party structures, the movement can keep its mobilisation focused and responsive to local realities. This coordinated effort will turn readiness into action, action into mobilisation and mobilisation into victory. Adamawa is ready. The structure is in place. The mission is achievable. One State. One Purpose. A Shared Commitment to Renewed Hope. With Fintiri as the leader, Adamawa will deliver, Insha Allah!

item.title: Nigeria joins league of nations in global measurement pact
item.description: By Adaobi Abimbola Nigeria has joined the league of nations with globally recognised measurement standards following the signing of the Mutual Recognition Arrangement of the International Committee for Weights and Measures, CIPM MRA, in France. The agreement was signed by the Director-General of the Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, Dr Ifeanyi Chukwunonso Okeke, at the 28th General Conference on Weights and Measures CGPM. The signing coincided with the DG’s third anniversary in office. According to a statement made by SON’s Director of Corporate Affairs, Mrs. Ethan Talatu, Nigeria’s admission as an Associate State of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, BIPM, took effect on June 4, 2026. The CIPM MRA is the framework through which national metrology institutes prove that their measurement standards are equivalent and earn global recognition for their calibration and measurement certificates. Okeke said that the arrangement would bring international recognition of Nigeria’s measurement capabilities, global acceptance of its calibration certificates and easier trade across borders. He added that it would reduce dependence on foreign metrology services, strengthen SON’s technical authority and open doors to scientific collaboration and capacity building. Nigeria now joins Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, South Africa and Tunisia as the only African countries with full BIPM membership. For manufacturers and small businesses, products can be tested locally and trusted abroad without the cost of foreign laboratories. item.title: FG targets $7.1bn sugar investments, 110,000 jobs in 10 years
item.description: The Federal Government is targeting $7.1 billion in investments in the sugar industry over 10 years to boost domestic production above two million metric tonnes annually, create 110,000 jobs and save $2.1 billion in foreign exchange annually. The programme, coordinated by the National Sugar Development Council (NSDC), is aimed at reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported raw sugar through increased sugarcane cultivation, processing capacity and private-sector investment. Executive Secretary of NSDC, Kamar Bakrin, disclosed the plan in Abuja, saying the initiative would strengthen local production and supporting agricultural infrastructure. Under the programme, the council is proposing 10 integrated sugar estates across Niger, Kwara, Oyo, Kaduna, Jigawa, Bauchi, Nasarawa and Adamawa states. The estates are expected to cover 143,478 hectares, with a combined milling capacity of 55,500 metric tonnes of sugarcane daily. According to NSDC, the proposed estates could produce 835,000 metric tonnes of sugar annually, while existing operators are expected to contribute another 1.22 million tonnes through increased output. The projects are also expected to support ethanol production and electricity generation, creating additional opportunities for agro-processing and value addition. To finance the programme, the council is seeking $5 billion in long-term debt and $2.1 billion in equity contributions from investors. Funding is expected to involve export credit agencies, development finance institutions and local financial organisations. NSDC also disclosed a $1 billion agreement with Chinese engineering company Sinomach, although the associated financing arrangements are yet to be completed. It is collaborating with the Bank of Industry on a proposed N10 billion Sugar Projects Acceleration Fund to support feasibility studies and prepare projects for investment.
